rationale.correct: Tags attach metadata to resources so that cost and ownership can be sliced after the fact. They cut across the containment hierarchy instead of replacing it, which is exactly what chargeback needs here: the resource groups stay organized by environment, and the cost report is grouped by the business-unit dimension the tag carries.

distractors.A: Rebuilding the hierarchy around one reporting need is the move the operations team ruled out, and it trades a structure the team relies on for a dimension that metadata already supplies.
distractors.C: A role assignment decides who may act on a resource. It authorizes access and carries no cost dimension, so shared groups stay unattributed.
distractors.D: An even split is an assumption rather than a measurement. The units draw on the shared groups unequally, so the report would charge costs to units that never incurred them.

questions.question: A textile mill's compliance officer must find where customer design files containing personal data have spread across the mill's storage accounts and file shares, label them by sensitivity, and keep track of them as copies move between systems. The security posture of the infrastructure holding them was reviewed separately and is not in question.

options.A: Microsoft Purview, to discover the data, map where it sits and classify it wherever it travels
options.B: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, to raise the security posture of the storage accounts holding the files
options.C: Azure Policy, to deny the creation of any storage account outside the mill's approved configuration
options.D: A published data-handling notice telling staff which locations may and may not hold personal data

rationale.correct: Governing the data estate is a different job from governing the resource estate the data happens to sit on. Microsoft Purview discovers, maps, classifies and protects sensitive information wherever it travels, which is the only approach here that follows the design files themselves rather than the accounts and services beneath them.

distractors.B: Defender for Cloud works on the security posture and regulatory compliance of the infrastructure. It hardens the accounts that hold the files and never looks inside them.
distractors.C: A policy governs what may be created and how it must be configured. It sets rules for the containers, and classifies nothing that lands in them.
distractors.D: A notice states where personal data is supposed to live. It documents an intention, and discovers, labels and tracks nothing.

questions.question: A veterinary clinic network is committed to keeping client records inside two approved regions. Engineers at each practice deploy their own resources, and last quarter two test databases turned up in a third region and had to be removed afterwards. The network wants any future deployment outside the approved regions refused at the moment of creation.

options.A: Apply a lock at each subscription so that resources cannot be created in the regions that are not approved
options.B: Withdraw deployment rights from the practice engineers and route every deployment through the central team
options.C: Assign a policy that permits only the two approved regions, so a deployment elsewhere is refused
options.D: Report monthly on resources by region and remove anything found outside the two approved ones

rationale.correct: Azure Policy is the deployment-time gate: what compliant looks like is defined once as a rule over a scope, and a resource that violates it is prevented from being created anywhere in that scope. Restricting the regions in which resources may be deployed is the canonical case, and it holds whoever issues the deployment and whichever surface they issue it from.

distractors.A: A resource lock protects resources that already exist from deletion or modification. It guards what is there and takes no part in deciding what may be created.
distractors.B: Centralizing every deployment removes the engineers' ability to work instead of making their deployments compliant, and a central team can put a database in the wrong region just as easily.
distractors.D: A monthly report finds the stray deployment after client records have already landed outside the approved regions — the same after-the-fact removal the network is trying to stop.

questions.question: A wind farm maintenance company adopted a standard this year: every resource carries an owner tag and sits in one of its approved regions. Most of the estate predates the standard. Leadership wants both a list of which existing resources fall short of it and assurance that the same standard holds for everything deployed from now on.

options.A: Azure Advisor's operational excellence recommendations, read across the whole of the existing estate
options.B: Assign the policy at the subscription and read its compliance state, which evaluates existing resources as well as new ones
options.C: Because a policy takes effect only on deployments made after it is assigned, redeploy the older resources through a template that meets the standard
options.D: An alert rule that fires whenever a resource is found sitting outside the standard the company adopted

rationale.correct: Azure Policy does two jobs over one estate. It gates new deployments, and it evaluates the resources that already exist against the same definition, reporting each of them as compliant or not. Assigning the definition at a scope that contains the older estate therefore produces the shortfall list and the ongoing enforcement from a single control.

distractors.A: Advisor recommends improvements drawn from general best practice. It does not evaluate an estate against a standard this company wrote, and it enforces nothing.
distractors.C: The premise is wrong: an assigned policy evaluates the resources already inside its scope and reports their compliance state, so nothing has to be redeployed to see the shortfall.
distractors.D: An alert notifies once a condition has been observed in telemetry. It is the notification layer, not an evaluation of resources against a compliance definition.

questions.question: A county courthouse system keeps its case-record storage account in a resource group that four administrators own. During a cleanup last year one of those owners deleted the wrong storage account. The clerk wants the record store protected so that even an owner cannot delete it without a deliberate, separate step first.

options.A: Apply a delete lock to the storage account, so deletion is refused for every principal until the lock is removed
options.B: Reduce the four administrators from owner to a role that carries fewer permissions on the resource group
options.C: Assign a policy to the resource group that denies the deletion of any storage account inside it
options.D: Turn on an activity log for the resource group so that a deletion is recorded against whoever performed it

rationale.correct: A resource lock blocks deletion or modification independently of who holds permissions. It stops an owner exactly as it stops anyone else, and the guarded action can only proceed once the lock has been deliberately removed — which is the separate step the clerk is asking for.

distractors.B: Changing role assignments changes who is authorized to act. A contributor can still delete a storage account, and the case records would be protected only by whoever holds the next role up.
distractors.C: A policy governs what may be created and how resources must be configured. The action to be stopped here is the deletion of something that already exists, which is the lock's job.
distractors.D: An activity log names who deleted the case records once they are gone. Recording a deletion is not refusing one.

questions.question: An insurance brokerage is placing four governance requirements against the control that meets each one. For each requirement below, select the control. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: No resource may be created outside the brokerage's two approved regions, whoever issues the deployment.
The claims database must survive a cleanup: nobody, not even a subscription owner, may delete it until the guard on it is deliberately removed.
Claims analysts must be able to read everything in the reporting resource group and change none of it.
Every virtual machine created from now on must carry a cost-center tag, or the deployment is refused.

rationale.correct: Three control classes answer three different questions. Azure Policy gates what may be created: a deployment is evaluated against a rule over its scope and refused when it does not comply, which is what both the region restriction and the mandatory cost-center tag need. A resource lock protects what already exists — it blocks deletion or modification regardless of permission, so it stops an owner too, and it has to be removed deliberately before the guarded action can proceed. Azure role-based access control (RBAC) decides who may attempt an action at all, which is the instrument for granting read without change. Only a lock stops an owner deleting; only a policy refuses a non-compliant creation; only a role assignment decides who may try.

questions.question: A coffee roastery chain manages its whole Azure estate by hand in the Azure portal. Its cloud lead wants to keep the portal for the work it genuinely suits and move everything else to surfaces better matched to it. Which piece of work should stay in the portal?

options.A: Building each new roasting site's resource set by hand from a written checklist, so the steps stay familiar to the team
options.B: Applying one configuration change to every site's resources in turn, with the administrator reopening each resource afterwards to confirm it landed
options.C: Keeping the definition of what a site should look like as a library of screenshots a reviewer approves before an administrator applies it
options.D: Exploring an unfamiliar subscription during a support call: seeing how its resources relate and reading one resource's metrics chart

rationale.correct: The portal is the graphical control plane, and it is at its best for exploration, visualization and one-off administration: looking over an estate somebody else built, reading a chart, changing one setting once. What it is wrong for is work that must be repeatable, reviewable or performed at scale, because a sequence of clicks cannot be versioned, compared or replayed identically.

distractors.A: A checklist is what teams reach for when the build should have been repeatable. Identical environments come from a definition that is deployed, not from a human following steps.
distractors.B: A change applied across an estate belongs to a surface that can iterate over resources. Reopening each resource in the same sitting that changed it also checks the work from inside the context that produced it.
distractors.C: Screenshots record what somebody intended to build. A reviewer can approve them and still cannot tell whether the estate matches, because the picture is not the thing that gets deployed.

questions.question: A ferry operator's duty manager has to run one short administrative command from a shared terminal in the port office. Nothing may be installed on that machine and no credentials may be stored on it, and the manager is already signed in to the company's browser session. Which surface fits the constraint?

options.A: The Azure CLI, installed on the port office terminal because it is the cross-platform command language
options.B: Azure Cloud Shell, opened in the browser and already authenticated for the manager's session
options.C: The Azure portal, stepping through the equivalent setting by hand on the resource's own page
options.D: A request to the central platform team asking them to run the command on the duty manager's behalf

rationale.correct: Azure Cloud Shell is the browser-hosted, pre-authenticated shell: it needs nothing installed on the machine in front of the user and leaves no credentials there, and it runs either of the two command languages — the cross-platform Azure CLI or the object-based Azure PowerShell. The constraint here is about where the shell runs and how it authenticates, not about which language the command is written in.

distractors.A: The Azure CLI is a command language and it is genuinely cross-platform. Installing it is the one thing the terminal forbids, and the same commands run in the browser-hosted shell with no install at all.
distractors.C: The portal can make the change and is the graphical surface, not a command one. It gives the duty manager a sequence of clicks where a command was asked for.
distractors.D: Handing the command to another team postpones a task the duty manager is authorized to perform and that a browser-hosted shell already makes possible.

questions.question: A container shipping line runs half its servers on-premises in two port datacenters and a few more with another cloud provider, and a berth-side contract prevents any of them moving this year. The governance team wants those servers inventoried alongside the Azure ones and covered by the same policy assignments.

options.A: Migrate the port servers into Azure first, and then govern the whole estate natively from there
options.B: A site-to-site connection between the two port datacenters and the shipping line's Azure virtual network
options.C: Azure Arc, which projects the non-Azure servers into Azure so the same management tooling governs them
options.D: Azure Monitor collecting metrics from the port servers into the same workspace as the Azure resources

rationale.correct: Azure Arc extends Azure's management plane to what does not run in Azure: on-premises and other-cloud machines are projected into Azure, appear in its inventory, and are governed with the same tooling — policy assignments included — as native resources. The requirement is management reach across the boundary, not connectivity across it and not migration through it.

distractors.A: Moving the servers is what the berth-side contract rules out this year. It answers a governance requirement by removing the constraint the team was told to work within.
distractors.B: A network connection makes the port servers reachable. Reachability is not management: the servers still appear in no Azure inventory and no policy can be assigned to them.
distractors.D: Collecting metrics gives the governance team observation of the port servers. Observation is not governance, and a metric stream carries no policy assignment.

questions.question: A glass recycling plant's platform team builds each processing line's environment by hand, and the environments have drifted apart. The team is adopting infrastructure as code. Which TWO things does that change actually buy it? (Select TWO.)

options.A: It removes the need for a separate approval step, as the deployment tool validates the definition before it runs
options.B: The environment is declared once and deployed repeatedly, so every processing line comes out identical
options.C: Responsibility for what the environments contain moves to the platform provider, which applies the definition
options.D: The estate becomes self-correcting: a resource that drifts from the definition is returned to it with nobody acting
options.E: The definition is a versioned artifact, so a proposed change can be reviewed and approved before it reaches the estate

rationale.correct: Infrastructure as code replaces clicking an environment into existence with declaring it. What that buys is repeatability — the same definition deploys the same environment every time — and reviewability, because a versioned artifact can be read, compared and approved before anything reaches the estate. Drift becomes visible for the same reason: there is now a written statement of what the estate should be to compare it against.

distractors.A: Validation checks that a definition is well formed. Whether the change it describes is the right one is the question an approval step exists to answer.
distractors.C: Declaring an estate does not move responsibility for its contents. The plant still owns what it deploys, in a definition exactly as it did in the portal.
distractors.D: Seeing drift and closing it are different things. The definition makes the difference visible, and correcting it is still a deployment somebody chooses to run.

questions.question: A cruise line's operations team changes its Azure estate from three directions: the portal, a deployment pipeline that calls the command line, and scripts run by administrators. An auditor asks how one set of permissions and policy rules can possibly hold when three different surfaces are issuing the changes.

options.A: Every one of those surfaces sends its request to Azure Resource Manager, the control plane where permissions and policy are applied
options.B: Each surface — the portal, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell — applies its own copy of the permission and policy rules, so the three configurations have to be kept aligned
options.C: Standardize on one surface and withdraw the other two, leaving a single path by which the estate can be changed
options.D: Enable a separate log on each of the three surfaces and reconcile those logs with one another every month

rationale.correct: Azure Resource Manager is the control plane that every deployment and management request goes through, whatever surface issued it — portal, command line or script. Authentication, role assignments and policy are evaluated there, once, which is why consistency does not depend on the tool an administrator happened to pick. The same control plane accepts ARM templates, the declarative format that makes a repeated deployment identical.

distractors.B: There are no per-surface copies of the rules to keep aligned. The surfaces are clients of one control plane and carry no enforcement of their own.
distractors.C: Removing tools narrows how the team can work without changing where enforcement happens, and the surface left standing is evaluated exactly as the two withdrawn ones were.
distractors.D: Reconciling logs describes afterwards what was allowed through. Consistency here is a property of where requests are evaluated, not of how their records are compared.

questions.question: A heavy machinery importer's new cloud lead inherits an estate nobody has reviewed for two years. The board asks for a prioritized list of improvements — cheaper, safer, more reliable — derived from how these particular resources are actually configured rather than from a generic checklist.

options.A: The pricing calculator, priced against the sizes the estate runs today, to show the board where money could be saved
options.B: Azure Advisor, which analyzes the resources that exist and returns personalized recommendations across those categories
options.C: A policy assignment across the subscription, reporting which resources fall short of the importer's own standards
options.D: Microsoft Defender for Cloud's secure score, taken as the answer to the whole of the board's improvement question

rationale.correct: Azure Advisor produces personalized best-practice recommendations across cost, security, reliability, performance and operational excellence, and it produces them by analyzing the resources that already exist. That is what separates a recommender from an estimator, which prices a design nobody has built, and from an enforcer, which decides what is allowed. The board asked for advice about this estate, so the surface that reads this estate is the one that answers.

distractors.A: Pricing a configuration estimates what something would cost. It reads no resource's actual configuration and recommends nothing about security or reliability.
distractors.C: A policy reports compliance against rules the importer wrote. It enforces a standard instead of proposing improvements, and it is silent on everything the standard does not mention.
distractors.D: Defender for Cloud covers security posture in depth and stops there. Cost, reliability and performance sit outside it, and the board asked about all four.

questions.question: Midway through a tournament an e-sports league's match service stops responding. Before touching its own code, the league wants to establish whether Azure is having an incident that affects the services and regions its own subscription depends on.

options.A: The public Azure Status page, which reports incidents affecting the platform overall
options.B: Resource health for the match service's virtual machine, which reports that one machine's own health
options.C: Azure Service Health, which reports incidents and planned maintenance for this subscription's services and regions
options.D: An alert rule on the match service's response time, which fires whenever responses slow beyond the configured threshold

rationale.correct: Three questions about one outage have three surfaces. Whether the platform is having an incident at all is the public status view; whether an incident touches the services and regions this subscription uses is Azure Service Health; and whether one particular resource is healthy is that resource's own health view. The league is asking the middle question, which is the personalized one.

distractors.A: The public view answers whether anything anywhere is wrong. It is not filtered to this subscription, so a page listing no broad incident still leaves the league's own regions unanswered.
distractors.B: Resource health is the right family at the wrong level. It describes one machine, and cannot say whether a regional service the league depends on is degraded.
distractors.D: An alert reports that the league's own service is slow, which is the symptom already in front of them. It says nothing about whether a platform incident is the cause.

questions.question: An orchestra and concert hall runs ticketing, door access and building-sensor workloads across many Azure resources. Each team reads its own resource's telemetry in isolation, and when ticketing slowed last week nobody could line that up against what the rest of the estate was doing. The venue wants one place that collects metrics and logs from all of those resources and can act on what they show.

options.A: Log Analytics on its own, as the workspace in which collected log data is queried
options.B: Application Insights, as the telemetry surface for what happens inside the ticketing application
options.C: A portal dashboard for each team, pinned with the charts for that team's own resources
options.D: Azure Monitor, the platform that collects, correlates and acts on telemetry from the whole estate

rationale.correct: Azure Monitor is the telemetry platform for the estate: it collects metrics and logs from many resources, correlates them in one place, and acts on what it finds. The named surfaces beneath it are parts of that platform rather than rivals to it — one is where collected data is queried, another reports what happens inside an application — so an estate-wide collection and correlation requirement is answered by the platform itself.

distractors.A: Querying is one job inside the platform. A workspace answers questions of data that something else collected, and does not itself gather the venue's estate-wide telemetry or act on it.
distractors.B: Application Insights sits at the application level and reports what happens inside one application. The requirement spans door access and building sensors as much as ticketing.
distractors.C: Per-team dashboards are what the venue already has in effect: each team watches its own resources, which is exactly the isolation that stopped anyone correlating the slowdown.

questions.question: A mining equipment supplier already collects log data from its Azure estate into one workspace. After a delivery-tracking failure an engineer wants to interrogate what was collected — which requests failed, on which resources, in the twenty minutes around the failure — and to refine the question as the answers come back.

options.A: Log Analytics, the surface on which collected log data is queried and analyzed
options.B: An alert rule on the failed-request signal, set to fire when failures cross a threshold
options.C: Application Insights, instrumenting the delivery-tracking application so the data is gathered again
options.D: Azure Advisor's operational excellence recommendations for the resources that were involved

rationale.correct: Log Analytics is the query surface: the place where log data that has already been collected is interrogated and analyzed, question by question, as an investigation narrows. It is neither the pipeline that gathers the telemetry nor the layer that notifies somebody about it — those are separate jobs inside the same platform.

distractors.B: An alert rule watches a signal for a condition and tells somebody when it is met. It notifies; it does not let an engineer ask a new question of data already collected.
distractors.C: Instrumenting the application adds another source of telemetry, and the supplier's data is already in the workspace. Collecting again answers nothing about what was collected then.
distractors.D: Advisor returns recommendations about how resources are configured. The engineer needs the specific events around one failure, which no recommendation contains.

questions.question: A bicycle-share operator's docking-station service degrades quietly: the queue of unprocessed dock events climbs for an hour before riders begin reporting problems. Operations wants to be told the moment queue depth crosses its agreed threshold, and wants the processing job restarted when that happens.

options.A: A saved Log Analytics query over the queue-depth data, run by an engineer at the start of each day
options.B: A wall-screen dashboard in the operations room showing queue depth as it rises and falls
options.C: Change the daily service summary into an hourly one so that the climb shows up sooner
options.D: An Azure Monitor alert on the queue-depth signal, firing at the threshold and triggering the restart

rationale.correct: Azure Monitor alerts are the notification-and-action layer: a rule watches a signal for a stated condition, fires when the condition is met, and can trigger a response as well as telling somebody. Storing telemetry and querying it are separate jobs, and neither of them reaches out when a threshold is crossed.

distractors.A: A saved query answers the question when somebody runs it. Overnight the queue climbs with nothing watching, which is the gap operations described.
distractors.B: A dashboard shows the climb to whoever happens to be looking. Observation is not notification, and nothing on a screen restarts the processing job.
distractors.C: An hourly summary shortens the wait and keeps its shape: the operator still learns after the fact and still has to act by hand.

questions.question: A motorcycle dealership network's booking site is slow for some customers, while every metric on the virtual machines, disks and network beneath it sits well inside normal. The team needs to see which requests inside the booking application are failing or running long, and which pages customers actually reach.

options.A: Azure Monitor metrics for the underlying virtual machines and disks, read over a longer window
options.B: Log Analytics queries over the platform logs already collected from those same resources
options.C: Application Insights, the application surface of the telemetry platform, which reports request failures and usage
options.D: Move the booking site onto a larger virtual machine size so that the slow requests complete sooner

rationale.correct: Application-level telemetry sits at a different altitude from platform-level collection. Request failures, performance anomalies and how customers actually use the pages happen inside the application, and Application Insights is the surface of the telemetry platform that reports them. The infrastructure beneath looks healthy precisely because the problem is not at that level.

distractors.A: Platform metrics describe the machines and disks the application runs on, which the team has already found healthy. A longer window shows more of the same level.
distractors.B: Querying platform logs interrogates telemetry gathered from the infrastructure. The failing requests were never in that data, so no query over it returns them.
distractors.D: More capacity answers a resource constraint, and the resources are not constrained. The slow requests would stay slow on a larger machine, and stay undiagnosed.
